title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is part of the 1986 'Analysis situs (troisième mouture)'. Grothendieck is building a point-free, combinatorial axiomatics for tame ('modéré') spaces. A set M of 'pieces' (cells or regions) carries three primitive relations, fixed on p.102:
- X ≤ Y, inclusion;
- X ≪ Y, 'well inside' or relatively-compact inclusion, with a variant X °≪ Y, 'inside the interior';
- X |∘| Y, separation: disjoint interiors, or not touching.
Further notation:
- ~X is the closed downset of X.
- L = ~X ∩ ~Y is the largest common closed part.
- Omb(L) is the 'shadow' of L.
- The derived relation X ≭ Y means 'X and Y meet cleanly / in general position'. It is defined by: every X' ∈ ~X∖L is |∘| every Y' ∈ ~Y∖L. In other words, outside their common closed part, X and Y are separated.
- X ∥ Y means X ≭ Y and L = ∅, i.e. completely separated.

This page.
(1) Axiom Mag 5''. The relation |∘| is symmetric and antireflexive (X |∘| Y implies Y |∘| X and X ≠ Y). It is also hereditary under interior shrinking: X |∘| Y, X' °≪ X and Y' °≪ Y imply X' |∘| Y'.
(2) Deduction of the old axiom Mag 5: if X ≭ Y and Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y, then there is Z' ∈ M with Z ≪ Z' ≤ X, Y. In effect, the 'common part' of two cleanly meeting pieces is realised by a single piece.
- By Mag M3 there are X' ∈ ~X and Y' ∈ ~Y with Z °≪ X' and Z °≪ Y'.
- If X' |∘| Y' held, heredity would give Z |∘| Z, contradicting antireflexivity.
- Hence X', Y' cannot both lie outside L. The remaining comparability, written 'X' ≤ Y'' and attributed to a strengthened Mag M5, should follow from this.
- The corollary of Mag 4'' (two distinct cleanly-meeting pieces are |∘|) then forces X' = Y'. This is the required Z'.
(3) Since ≭ is now in hand, so is ∥. Proposition 1: X ∥ Y iff X' |∘| Y' for all X' ∈ ~X and Y' ∈ ~Y. This is immediate from the definitions, since L = ∅.
(4) Proposition 2, 'AtC (spec)', condition C. It characterises clean intersection by shrinkings. X ≭ Y iff X' ∥ Y' for all X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y whose traces on the shadow of L are empty (X'_L = ~X' ∩ Omb(L) = ∅ and Y'_L = ∅). In words: X and Y meet cleanly iff anything well inside them and away from their common part is completely separated.
- ⇒ is expected always to hold. The next page proves it via Mag 5''.
- ⇐ is expected to need an extra axiom of type AtL1, 'divisibilité infinie' (infinite divisibility, i.e. no atoms).
- The next page reformulates it as: X ≭ Y iff x ∥ y for all x ∈ comb(X)°, y ∈ comb(Y)°.

Purpose: replacing the earlier axiom Ab L3 by Mag 4''/5'', and deriving the earlier Mag axioms, in a region-based foundation of tame topology.
errors: In Mag 5'' the conclusion is written 'implique X|∘|Y'. It must be X'|∘|Y' (heredity under °≪).

In the proof of Mag 5, the step 'by Mag M5 (just strengthened) we get X' ≤ Y'' is elliptic. The real mechanism is the contrapositive of Mag 5'' (Z |∘| Z is impossible), combined with the definition of ≭, to force X', Y' into L. Comparability is not justified explicitly.
The proof uses X' ∈ ~X with Z °≪ X'. This tacitly needs Mag M3 to provide °≪ (interior) rather than ≪, which matches the deleted 'OPS' line.
Proposition 2 is marked '(?)'. The converse depends on an axiom (AtL1, infinite divisibility) not yet stated, so on this page it is a conjecture.
The subscripts in 'X'_{?} ∥ Y'_{?}' are crossed out. The intended conclusion is simply X' ∥ Y' (confirmed on the next page).

ideas.what: Point-free axiomatics of 'pieces' with primitive relations ≤ (part), ≪ (well inside) and |∘| (separated), to found tame topology
ideas.modern_name: mereotopology / region-based topology; proximity spaces with strong inclusion ≪; contact algebras; RCC (non-tangential proper part)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna (1920s); Efremovič (proximity, 1951); Clarke (1981); Randell–Cui–Cohn RCC (1992); Vakarelov, Düntsch (contact algebras, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for 'topologie modérée' but gives no such axiomatics

ideas.what: Derived relation ≭: two pieces meet cleanly iff, outside their largest common closed part, everything is separated
ideas.modern_name: clean intersection / general position of strata; regular (frontier-condition) stratifications expressed relationally
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom stratification theory (frontier condition); not usually expressed point-free

ideas.what: Mag 5'': separation is symmetric, irreflexive and hereditary under interior shrinking
ideas.modern_name: axioms of a disjointness/separation relation in contact algebras (the complement of the contact relation)

ideas.what: Characterisation of clean intersection by complete separation of all shrinkings avoiding the shadow of the common part (condition C), with the converse needing an infinite-divisibility axiom
ideas.modern_name: 'atomless' or density axiom in Boolean contact algebras; normality of proximity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Düntsch–Winter, Vakarelov et al. (atomless contact algebras)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 tame-topology foundation is a mereotopology: regions with part, well-inside and separation relations, plus an infinite-divisibility axiom. This closely parallels the later region-connection/contact-algebra literature (RCC 1992; Düntsch, Vakarelov) and proximity theory. That literature never cites it, and the tame-topology/o-minimal literature never took the point-free route.
missed.quote: un axiome supplémentaire genre AtL1 (axiome de divisibilité infinie)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a point-free (locale-like) axiomatisation of o-minimal or semi-algebraic stratified spaces, bridging o-minimality and qualitative spatial reasoning.

missed.claim: Proposition 2 (clean intersection iff complete separation of all shrinkings away from the shadow of the common part) is left conditional on an unformulated divisibility axiom.
missed.quote: ⇒ sûrement toujours vrai, et ⇐ moyennant un axiome supplémentaire genre AtL1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It asks for the minimal axioms under which 'general position' is detectable by separation of interiors. This is an open-ended foundational question for region-based tame topology.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine axiom-juggling step. Its interest is that Grothendieck's unpublished Analysis situs is a genuine point-free, mereotopological foundation for tame topology, with 'well-inside', separation and divisibility axioms, and it seems unrecognised by both the o-minimal and the mereotopology communities. No finished striking theorem appears on this page itself.
